answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a time-staked bond: each identity locks funds that vest slowly over a long voyage of verified work, so spinning up many fake agents multiplies both the locked capital and the waiting time. A reputation plume, a public trail of completed tasks, grows only through consistent on-time performance, like a lotus that opens gradually and cannot be forced overnight. An attacker pays the full bond and delay per identity, while an honest agent amortizes one bond across years of work.
